Arsenal survive Mansfield Town scare to reach FA Cup quarter-finals with 2-1 win

Gunners boss Mikel Arteta made nine changes to the side that beat Brighton & Hove Albion 1-0 in midweek to open up a seven-point lead at the top of the English Premier League. Noni Madueke put the 14-time FA Cup winners ahead against the League One strugglers shortly before half-time, only for substitute Will Evans to level shortly after the break. Evans told TNT Sports: “I wanted to prove a point today - not just to the team but to myself as well. It’s typical isn’t it, for me to have a league goal drought and then come on for a half against Arsenal and have a goal against them.”
The game opened up, with chances for both sides before substitute Eberechi Eze thumped home to restore Arsenal’s lead. Eze told TNT Sports: “It was a difficult environment to play in. But we did what we had to do and we are through to next round which is the important thing. “We are working hard and we are focussing on the process. Otherwise, we won’t get there. We are working hard and doing everything we can to win all the silverware on offer.”
Max Dowman became the Gunners’ youngest-ever FA Cup player, starting at the age of 16 years and 66 days and there was also a starting place for 16-year-old Marli Salmon as Arteta shuffled his resources. import sys, json, csv
sys.path.insert(0,'memory')
from forecasts import F

# Load valid qids
with open('market.csv') as f:
    valid = {r['qid'] for r in csv.DictReader(f)}

# Clean: drop 0.0 and empty-string outcomes, verify qids valid
clean = {}
issues = []
for q, o in F.items():
    if q not in valid:
        issues.append(f"INVALID QID {q}")
        continue
    no = {k: round(v,4) for k, v in o.items() if v > 1e-9 and k.strip()}
    if len(no) == 0:
        issues.append(f"EMPTY after clean {q}")
        continue
    clean[q] = no

# any valid qids missing?
missing = valid - set(clean.keys())
print("Issues:", issues[:10])
print("Missing from forecast:", missing)

# Save JSON
with open('memory/forecasts.json','w') as f:
    json.dump(clean, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=0)
print("Exported", len(clean), "forecasts to memory/forecasts.json")
# Show distribution of number of outcomes
from collections import Counter
print("Outcome counts:", Counter(len(o) for o in clean.values()))
# Show a few sums
import statistics
sums = [sum(o.values()) for o in clean.values()]
print(f"Prob sum: min={min(sums):.2f} max={max(sums):.2f} mean={statistics.mean(sums):.2f}")
PYEOF

## Scoring reminder

- Sports specific scorers → top 3-5 team scorers, spread.
- "Which city/state/country" unpredictable → geographic plausibility spread.
- Diplomacy/appointments → most plausible named official, spread.
- Tech → naming-convention reasoning.
